picks.title: From Uganda to the Dalai Lama: The Chronicles of an African Seeker in India | Bhante Buddharakkhita
picks.summary:
In this talk, Bhante Buddharakkhita, visiting from Uganda, speaks about his journey from Africa  into Buddhism, and how the first four blessings described by the Buddha in the Maṇgala Sutta (Discourse on Blessings - https://www.dhammatalks.org/books/ChantingGuide/Section0051.html) can help keep us on the path. Learn more at https://bhantebuddharakkhita.org/ and https://ugandabuddhistcenter.org/



Bio

Bhante first encountered Buddhism in 1990 while studying and living in India. He was ordained as a Buddhist monk by the late Most Venerable U Silananda in 2002 at the Tathagata Meditation Center
picks.reason: A Buddhist monk shares his journey and teachings from the Mangala Sutta blessings.

picks.title: Ep. 295 – Caverly Morgan
picks.summary: Caverly Morgan joins Sharon for episode 295 of the Metta Hour Podcast to talk about her book, The Heart of Who We Are.Caverly Morgan is a teacher of awakening, nonprofit founder, speaker, and author who blends the original spirit of Zen with a modern nondual and relational approach. Her practice began in 1995 and has included eight years of training in a silent Zen monastery. She has been teaching contemplative practice since 2001. Caverly supports others in remembering our true nature—not through more techniques or self-improvement strategies, but through presence, inquiry, and togetherness.
picks.reason: A Zen teacher blends traditional and modern approaches to awakening and nature.

picks.title: The True Nature of Devotion In Our Lives
picks.summary: In this talk Samantabhadri explores what it was like to meet the Buddha, the fully Enlightened human being. She then discusses 'garava' as devotion for the whole richness of our Dharma Lives, including positive emotions for all beings. This talk was given on an Order weekend at  Taraloka Retreat Centre, 2022.  ***  Help us keep FBA Podcasts free for everyone! Donate now Subscribe to the FBA podcast: A full, curated, quality Dharma talk, every week. Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube
picks.reason: Talk on devotion and meeting the Buddha, exploring positive emotions in Dharma life.

picks.title: A Buddhist Guide to How to Truly Love with Maria Heim
picks.summary:
Maria Heim is a professor of religion at Amherst College. Her new book, How to Truly Love: An Ancient Guide to a Life of Kindness, presents a fresh and accessible translation of a chapter from the Path of Purification, a meditation manual by the great 5th-century sage Buddhaghosa. Through a careful exploration of the brahmaviharas, or sublime attitudes, Buddhaghosa offers practical strategies for releasing anger and hatred and finding freedom.

picks.reason: Maria Heim explores Buddhist brahmaviharas and strategies for kindness.

picks.title: Connecting with our Inner Buddha | Venerable Hue Can  | 4 September 2026
picks.summary: Venerable Hue Can is the Abbess of Sunyata Meditation Centre in Vic Park and has the very clear goal to teach others how to realize their full potential through Zen Buddhism. Venerable Hue Can had an interesting and diverse career as a teacher, Children’s Librarian and co-ordinator of the Ethnic Child Care Resource Unit. As an advocate for access and equity she have worked in the area of social welfare, particularly in the Vietnamese community in Western Australia. When the Most Venerable Master Thich Thanh Tu came to Perth in 1996 she was fortunate to attend his lecture “Why am I a Buddhist”.
picks.reason: A Zen abbess teaches how to realize potential through Zen Buddhist practice.

picks.title: A Neuroscientist’s Guide to Changing Your Brain with Dr. Richard Davidson
picks.summary: Your brain is changing all the time, whether you realize it or not. Everything from your hobbies and chores to the media you consume can physically shape it. So how can you make sure it’s changing in ways that actually serve you? Laurie speaks with neuroscientist Dr. Richard Davidson, whose decades of work with the Dalai Lama helped pioneer the scientific study of meditation. picks.reason: Neuroscientist discusses meditation's impact on the brain with Buddhist roots.

picks.title: Metta as an Ethical Practice
picks.summary:
Metta as an Ethical PracticeRoy Wyman explores metta, or loving-kindness, as a practical antidote to ill will, shame, reactivity, and self-hatred. picks.title: The Reset for Anxiety, Overthinking, and Losing Yourself in the Wrong Story | Diana Winston
picks.summary: A simple daily check-in you can do anywhere, a four-part practice for handling hard emotions, and a new way to relate to negative judgments. Plus, why transcendence is more accessible than you think. Diana Winston is the Director of UCLA Mindful, with three decades of experience teaching mindfulness for health and well-being. She has authored three books, including  The Little Book of Being, and has taught at Spirit Rock Meditation Center for 25 years. A founder of the International Mindfulness Teachers Association, she continues to guide individuals and organizations in cultivating awareness
picks.reason: Mindfulness teacher offers practical tools for anxiety and emotional resilience.

picks.title: Continuity of Mindfulness
picks.summary: We don't meditate to get good at meditation. Instead, our practice lays the ground for awareness which we, hopefully, carry throughout our days. Continuity of mindfulness is a phrase which conveys this idea. In this talk Mary talks about Thich Nhat Hanh's book, Peace is Every Breath, which brings practice down to the most mundane parts of our lives like brushing teeth and making breakfast. The sacred is right here all the time when we're aware.Recorded Sept. 12, 2026 in the virtual worldSend me a text with any questions or comments! Include your name and email if you would like a response - it
picks.reason: Talk on mindfulness continuity in daily life based on Thich Nhat Hanh's teachings.
